clips.caption:
A guy built a $200 million business from nothing, flipping pizzas while living in his mother-in-law's basement.

The business exploded — hundreds of employees, a huge new building, more locations every year. Kevin Trudeau's guest, tax attorney Mark Kohler, told him to pull some money out. He never did.

Every dollar went straight back into the company. When the market finally turned, the overhead was too high to survive it, and he walked away penniless.

Farmers call this "land rich, cash poor" — buying more land instead of ever banking a cushion.

It isn't about how big your business gets. It's whether you ever take anything off the table.

#kevintrudeau #smallbusiness #entrepreneur #wealthmindset #businessowner #taxstrategy

If you're getting paid $30 an hour at your job, you should be charging $75 to $100 an hour for the exact same skill — as your own boss.

Tax attorney Mark Kohler tells Kevin Trudeau a service business is the easiest place to start: low overhead, no inventory, and you already have the industry knowledge from your day job. Tour guides, landscapers, consultants, window cleaners — pick anything you're good at.

Once you triple your rate, the next move is hiring someone else at $30 an hour to do the work you're now charging $75 for.

What skill are you giving away for a fraction of what it's worth?

#kevintrudeau #sidehustle #smallbusiness #entrepreneur #wealthmindset #businessowner

Peter Thiel put five thousand dollars into a Roth IRA in 1999. It's worth five billion dollars today, and he'll never pay a dollar of tax on it.

Tax attorney Mark Kohler tells Kevin Trudeau this isn't reserved for billionaires — it's called the mega backdoor Roth, and there's no income limit that locks regular business owners out of it. His own clients run Roth accounts worth over a hundred million dollars, funded the same way.

Most people are told they make too much money to use one. That advice is decades out of date.

Is your accountant still working off 1980s rules?

#kevintrudeau #rothira #wealthmindset #taxstrategy #entrepreneur #financialfreedom

Kevin Trudeau's guest doesn't just hold stocks in his retirement accounts. He owns cattle in one.

Tax attorney Mark Kohler has a single-family rental inside his health savings account that paid for his kids' braces tax-free. Twenty Black Angus steers on a Utah ranch, inside another. Bitcoin and XRP in a Roth. A rental property in Illinois inside his IRA, cash-flowing every month without a tax bill.

It's called self-directing, and almost nobody knows retirement accounts can legally hold real assets like this, not just mutual funds.

What's sitting in your retirement account that could be working this hard?

#kevintrudeau #selfdirectedira #wealthmindset #taxstrategy #realestate #financialfreedom

Most people think they need an LLC before they can write anything off. Tax attorney Mark Kohler says that's flat wrong.

He tells Kevin Trudeau you don't need any entity to deduct your auto, your marketing costs or your team — you can do all of it as a sole proprietor, using nothing but your own name. Even a simple drive to a client meeting makes the gas and the meal deductible.

Forming an LLC or corporation is about how you structure a business you already have. It has nothing to do with whether you're allowed to save on taxes.

Have you been putting off a side hustle because you thought you needed paperwork first?

#kevintrudeau #smallbusiness #taxstrategy #sidehustle #entrepreneur #llc

Remember the old phrase, "a penny saved is a penny earned"? Tax attorney Mark Kohler tells Kevin Trudeau most business owners never actually feel it until they own something.

Working for other law firms, he never thought twice about the cost of paperclips or the copy machine — that was someone else's problem. The day he was about to buy new equipment for his own firm, it hit him: save a thousand dollars here, and he'd effectively made a thousand dollars this month.

Cutting a tax bill by a dollar is identical to earning that dollar, without doing any extra work to get it.

Where in your own business are you still spending like it's not your money?
